clue.text: Accustomed to being exploited

definitions.meaning: being familiar with or in the habit of something
taken advantage of, put to work for someone else's gain

explanation.surface: A complaint from someone long taken advantage of who no longer notices it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to one past participle: habituated to something, and employed or taken advantage of.

clue.text: Large bed ordered? Capital!

indicators.note: the letters of large and bed are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an outsized bed and exclaims 'Capital!' in delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' reads as an old-fashioned exclamation of approval, but it is the definition: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serbian city is the capital of Serbia, formerly of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Handy fencing implement

parts.note: the sword a fencer holds in the hand, disguised as a useful tool for putting up fences

explanation.surface: A useful gadget for building garden fences.
explanation.definitionFit: The light thrusting sword used in sport fencing is a held, hand-wielded weapon.

clue.text: Illegally transfers money from Arundel's refurbishment

indicators.note: a refurbishment rebuilds something, so the letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Dirty money is siphoned off from the restoration works at Arundel Castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Arundel is a town in West Sussex famous for its castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing criminal money through legitimate channels to hide its origin is the financial sense of cleaning it.

clue.text: What most fish have to be weighed on

definitions.meaning: the small protective plates covering a fish's skin

explanation.surface: An angler's riddle about what a catch possesses and what it is put on to be weighed.
explanation.definitionFit: The same plural noun names both the plates on a fish's skin and the balance used for weighing.

clue.text: New stars never cross

indicators.note: the letters of stars never are made new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: An astronomical claim that freshly formed stars never pass across one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a verb in the sentence but is an adjective: lying across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying crosswise, at right angles to an axis, is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Gloomy sergeant major has face put out

indicators.note: the face is put outside, around the sergeant major's letters

parts.note: a clock's face is its dial
SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant major

explanation.surface: A miserable sergeant major whose face looks put out, or annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as 'annoyed' but tells you the face goes outside the abbreviation, giving DI-SM-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary and depressing describe the same cheerless mood, a simple synonym.

clue.text: In certain charts it may indicate a mile

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the two words that follow, spanning their join

explanation.surface: A remark about map symbols and what they stand for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a plain preposition but signals the letters hiding across 'certain charts'; old maps were drawn at this small unit to the mile.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Ordnance Survey maps used a scale where one small imperial unit (2.54 cm) stood for a mile.

clue.text: Set new record that's very demanding

indicators.note: set is made new by shuffling its letters

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Setting a fresh record is a tough thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SET into STE, followed by EP.
explanation.definitionFit: A price or task that is excessive or hard is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Agreement to unit working the instrument

parts.note: an accord is an agreement
I is the Roman numeral for one, a unit
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Signing a deal to get a factory unit up and running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' suggests a legal document, given 'Agreement', but is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeezebox with bellows and keys is a musical instrument.

clue.text: In which a boxer may drop his guard?

definitions.text: In which a boxer may drop his guard?

parts.words: In which a boxer may drop his guard?
parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, and a guard dog can relax in its own shelter

explanation.surface: Where a prizefighter might lower his defences.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, not a fighter; a guard dog off duty rests in its hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small outdoor hut houses a pet hound, where it can rest from guard duty.

clue.text: Girl in New York taking speed

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A young woman in Manhattan on drugs, speed being amphetamine.
explanation.definitionFit: A beautiful young woman is poetically likened to a nature spirit of Greek myth.

clue.text: No longer plentiful, for instance

parts.note: ex- describes something no longer so, as in an ex-wife
ample means plentiful

explanation.surface: Something that used to be abundant, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance and a case in point are synonyms, illustrations of a general rule.

clue.text: Do well, taking about ninety fish

indicators.note: the fish takes the number in, wrapping round it

parts.note: an eel is a fish
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An angler succeeds by landing around ninety fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately' but works with 'taking' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine or be outstanding at something is to perform very well.

clue.text: Calling for a statement

definitions.meaning: a vocation or line of work
a declaration, as of faith or love

explanation.surface: Phoning someone to get a quote from them.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both one's occupation, a vocation, and an avowal, as in a declaration of faith.

clue.text: Sausage and veal cooked in sauce

indicators.note: the cooked veal goes inside the sauce

parts.note: soy is a sauce

indicators.note: veal is cooked into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A recipe: sausage and veal simmered in a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: A saveloy is a spicy red British sausage sold in fish-and-chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly seasoned smoked pork link is a type of sausage.

clue.text: Measures the mast beams

definitions.meaning: units of length of three feet
the spars hung across a ship's mast to carry the sails

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up the timbers of a ship's mast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the plural of a three-foot unit and the name for horizontal spars on a mast.

clue.text: Statement of faith many repeat

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to redo something is to do it again

explanation.surface: A declaration of belief that many people recite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many repeat' reads as congregations reciting, but it is C plus REDO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for 'I believe' opens the creed, so it names any set of beliefs.

clue.text: The German returns depressed

indicators.note: the German word is turned back to front

parts.note: das is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A German man comes home feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down, unhappy and low are synonyms.

clue.text: They fill much of their working days

definitions.text: They fill much of their working days

parts.words: They fill much of their working days
parts.note: people whose days are spent putting fillings in teeth

explanation.surface: Busy workers whose days are full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill' reads as occupying time, but the people fill cavities.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who drill and fill teeth spend their workday doing it.

clue.text: Clause added for a cyclist

definitions.meaning: an extra condition added to a contract or bill

explanation.surface: A contract term inserted for the benefit of a bike rider.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both an amendment appended to a document and one who sits astride a bike or horse.

clue.text: After a cover up, politician is shilly-shallying

indicators.note: the politician comes after the reversed letters
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician dithers after a cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover up' reads as a scandal, but 'up' turns 'a cover' backwards in this down clue, giving DILA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawdling and procrastinating mean the same as wavering indecisively.

clue.text: Fifty snakes — and their partners

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
adders are snakes

explanation.surface: Fifty snakes — and the board game where ladders go with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakes and ladders is a children's board game; the snakes' partners are the ladders.
explanation.definitionFit: In the board game the climbing pieces are paired with the serpents.

clue.text: God willing, it's all right to admit artist and composer

parts.note: DV stands for Deo volente, Latin for God willing
OK means all right
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist and a composer agree to be admitted, God willing.
explanation.walkthrough: D.V. (Deo volente) is a Latin tag often written on letters and invitations.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonín Dvořák was a Czech composer of the New World Symphony.

clue.text: Alcohol providing animation

definitions.meaning: strong liquor such as gin or whisky

explanation.surface: Drink as the source of liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: One noun covers both distilled liquor and liveliness or verve.

clue.text: Unnecessary loss of a point irritates

indicators.note: one compass letter is lost from the word

parts.note: needless means unnecessary
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Pointlessly dropping a point is annoying, as in a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: To goad or provoke someone is to annoy them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: They are bound to look better and last longer

definitions.text: They are bound to look better and last longer

parts.words: They are bound to look better and last longer
parts.note: volumes given hard covers by a bookbinder look smarter and survive longer

explanation.surface: A confident prediction that certain things will improve with time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as 'certain to' but means having a binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Volumes stitched into covers are bound, and a binding protects them.

clue.text: Cane provided by master

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster delivering a caning.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to thrash and to defeat, conquer or get the better of.

clue.text: Began by being made a member

definitions.meaning: admitted to a society, often with a ceremony

explanation.surface: Starting out as a new recruit to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both started something and formally admitted into a group.

clue.text: One on the front line in Russia?

definitions.text: One on the front line in Russia?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one is placed on top of the front line

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the van, short for vanguard, is the front line of an army

explanation.surface: A soldier serving at the front during a war in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a typical Russian soldier, nicknamed with the commonest Russian first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday Russian first name was soldiers' slang for any Russian infantryman.

clue.text: Mythological princess performed with nothing on

indicators.note: in a down clue, the zero is placed on, following, the verb

parts.note: did means performed
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A legendary princess who acted in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of Carthage in Virgil's Aeneid was a Tyrian princess of legend.

clue.text: An old philosopher now in charge of dissecting?

parts.note: an atomist, like Democritus, was an ancient Greek thinker holding that matter is made of atoms

explanation.surface: A thinker of antiquity reborn as a modern dissector.
explanation.walkthrough: The atomists split the world into atoms; the clue imagines one now cutting up bodies instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist of bodily structure dissects corpses to study them.

clue.text: Bill gets free bitter

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Someone let off a bill turns resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, pungent or caustic taste or smell is harsh and sour.
